work.problem: The Builder consults Kappa only when a prompt or handoff happens to send it there: no rule requires it before diagnosis, and nothing checks that it happened (Kappa-first, KAN-60 slice 3, read side).

findings.reason: Same class: a written journal rule with no check. Its correction (a check run on every PR, shown failing on fixtures) is the pattern: the Kappa-first rule ships with its check in the same PR.
findings.revalidation: The append-only check still runs in journal.yml on every PR (read at 0175fc2); the new check is a step in the same job and image, so the pattern applies unchanged.

findings.reason: Recurs F-0014: a journal rule (CAPA fields) whose preventive check was planned and never built. Lesson: do not merge the Kappa-first rule as text with the check left for later.

The design record had rules and a reference checker but no gate step that called them. Lesson: the reference retrieve() in harness_reference.py exists and is called by nothing; the new retrieval must be wired into a running workflow, not only tested.

lessons: Ship the rule and its check in one change, with designed-to-fail cases (F-0014, F-0027, F-0030).
Test the retrieval against real entries in both journal forms, not only the bold-list form (F-0089).
Mutate the checker after its tests pass; a passing suite can still miss a branch (F-0098).
Claim only what the check proves: completeness and order, not reasoning quality (F-0019).
A new boundary gets a versioned contract first (F-0022, F-0029).
uncertainty: Only Playbook pull requests are enforced by this change; the other repositories wait for the central gates.yml step.

The check verifies that the record existed before the first implementation commit, not that its first version was complete; a later update is allowed and only the final version is checked against current Kappa.
The query (rules and fingerprints) is chosen by the agent. Open findings in the component are always required, but a too-narrow query can leave out a closed finding that would have helped.
